statement: For every relative-error rounding model M and every finite binary tree T of real pairs, if (depth(T)+1)u<1, the actual rounded computation equals the exact sum of a tree of perturbed exact leaf products of the same shape. Each exact product x is replaced by y with |y-x| <= ((depth(T)+1)u/(1-(depth(T)+1)u))|x|. The computation rounds each leaf multiplication and each internal-node addition in the grouping specified by T. The existential perturbation concerns products, not the individual input factors.

targets.name: Research.BinaryTreeReduction.roundedDotProduct_exists_perturbation
targets.statement: For every M: Research.FloatingPoint.Model and T: Tree(R x R), write u=M.u, r=M.round, d=depth(T), and k=d+1 in N. If ku<1 (casting k to R), then there exists P: Tree(R) such that IsPerturbation(gamma(k,u),exactProductTree(T),P) and exactSum(P)=roundedDotProduct(M,T). Here gamma(k,u)=ku/(1-ku). Tree(A) consists of finite ordered binary trees generated by leaf(a), a in A, and node(L,R), L,R in Tree(A), with no empty-tree constructor. Depth is 0 at a leaf and 1+max(depth(L),depth(R)) at a node. For b in R, IsPerturbation(b,X,P) is the inductively defined relation with leaf case |y-x|<=b|x| for X=leaf(x), P=leaf(y), and node case requiring the relation for both corresponding children. Thus P has the same shape as the exact-product tree, and for every corresponding leaf (a,b) of T and y of P, |y-ab|<=gamma(k,u)|ab|. exactSum(leaf(y))=y and exactSum(node(L,R))=exactSum(L)+exactSum(R), with exact real addition. The right side is the constructed computation D_M(leaf(a,b))=r(ab), D_M(node(L,R))=r(D_M(L)+D_M(R)). The model parameters and rounding hypothesis are as specified in assumptions. The theorem specifies existence of P, not an algorithm choosing it or perturbed individual factors.

constructions.name: Research.BinaryTreeReduction.exactProductTree
constructions.description: A function Tree(R x R) -> Tree(R). For every input tree T, map each leaf pair (a,b) to the leaf with exact real value ab, preserving every internal node and the order of its children. Recursively E(leaf(a,b))=leaf(ab), E(node(L,R))=node(E(L),E(R)). This performs multiplication at leaves and no summation. It is the reference tree whose real leaf products are perturbed in the target theorem.

constructions.name: Research.BinaryTreeReduction.roundedProductTree
constructions.description: A function Model -> Tree(R x R) -> Tree(R). For every model M and tree T, map each leaf pair (a,b) to leaf(M.mul(a,b))=leaf(r(ab)), preserving the tree shape and child order. Recursively Q_M(node(L,R))=node(Q_M(L),Q_M(R)). It rounds each exact leaf product once and does no internal addition. It is the intermediate tree supplied to roundedSum by roundedDotProduct, and is not specified to be the existential perturbed tree P of the theorem.

constructions.name: Research.BinaryTreeReduction.roundedDotProduct
constructions.description: A function Model -> Tree(R x R) -> R, defined for every M and T by roundedSum(M,roundedProductTree(M,T)). For a real-valued tree S, roundedSum(M,leaf(x))=x and roundedSum(M,node(L,R))=M.add(roundedSum(M,L),roundedSum(M,R))=r(roundedSum(M,L)+roundedSum(M,R)). Consequently D_M(leaf(a,b))=r(ab) and D_M(node(L,R))=r(D_M(L)+D_M(R)). It returns a real obtained by rounding every leaf product and every internal-node addition in the original tree grouping. A single leaf returns its rounded product; the construction does not balance or rearrange the tree. Under the theorem hypothesis this output equals the exact sum of a same-shaped tree of perturbed exact products with the stated uniform relative bound.

assumptions: Universally quantified model M consists of u in R with 0<=u, a function r: R -> R, and the property: for every z in R there exists delta in R such that |delta|<=u and r(z)=z(1+delta). Delta may depend on z. No further rounding properties are supplied or assumed.

Universally quantified T is any finite nonempty ordered binary tree of real pairs, with exactly two children at each internal node. There is no balance hypothesis and no sign or nonzero restriction on its real entries.

The explicit theorem hypothesis is (depth(T)+1)u<1, where depth(leaf(a))=0 and depth(node(L,R))=1+max(depth(L),depth(R)). The natural number depth(T)+1 is cast to R in products with u. This hypothesis makes 1-(depth(T)+1)u positive.

The supplied definitions use real arithmetic: M.mul(a,b)=r(ab), M.add(a,b)=r(a+b), and gamma(k,u)=ku/(1-ku) for k in N and u in R. exactSum uses exact addition of leaf values. Mapping a function over a tree changes only its leaves.

The existential variable P is a real-valued tree. Its correspondence with the exact-product tree is imposed by IsPerturbation, whose bound is gamma(depth(T)+1,u). At each leaf, |y-ab|<=gamma(depth(T)+1,u)|ab|; hence a zero exact product has zero corresponding perturbed leaf. The exact sum of P must equal roundedDotProduct(M,T).
